newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan urges Burma to allow political rallies.
newsitem.headline: Japan urges Burma to allow political rallies.

text.p: Japan on Tuesday said it regretted moves by Burma's military government to block an opposition political rally and urged the Rangoon junta to permit political activities.
"The Japanese find these moves that run counter to democratisation regrettable," said top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama.
"We call on the government of Burma to properly recognise legitimate political activities," he told a news conference.

On Tuesday a small group of opposition leaders met at the home of National League for Democracy (NLD) party leader Aung San Suu Kyi after the military government refused to permit a large special gathering there.
The NLD had planned to celebrate the seventh anniversary of its landslide 1990 election victory which was not recognised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).

Last week after reports that the military government had detained scores of NLD members, Japan called for the release of all detainees and urged the SLORC to start serious dialogue with the opposition.
